steps.caption: White to move. Several queen checks are possible. Some end the game on the spot and some give the king a square. Before you go on, pick one you think is mate.

steps.prompt: Which check would you play, and what do you expect the black king to be able to do after it?

fields.label: My check, and what the king can do:

steps.text: **The question.** A queen can check a king in many ways, but only some checks end the game. By the end of this lesson you will test any queen check with three short questions, find a supported check in one move or two, and explain to a friend why one check mates at once while a near twin only draws or takes longer. Marks: [V] verified here, [I] inference, [H] a guess worth testing.

steps.caption: A mating check. The queen on h5 would also mate; the other checks give the king a square.

line.say: The queen checks along the h-file from far away. Her king covers g8 and g7, and the file covers h7. Nothing is left: checkmate.

steps.caption: The near twin: another check, one move slower.

line.say: This check looks just as forcing, and the queen eyes the corner. But it leaves a square.
Black has exactly one reply: the king steps to h7, the one square this check did not cover.
Now the queen lands beside the king on a square the white king protects: mate. The twin is slower, not wrong. It leaves one flight square, so mate takes two moves.

steps.caption: Black king g8, white king g6. The queen can check from far away or from right beside the king.

line.say: The queen lands beside the king, protected by the white king. Between them they cover every neighbouring square.

steps.caption: The kings face each other with one square between them. Nothing needs protecting, because the black king can never reach the queen.

line.say: A check from the far corner. The white king covers the three squares in front of the black king; the queen covers the rest of the rank.

steps.caption: Black to move. The colours are reversed, and now two different mates exist: one beside the king, one on the h-file.

line.say: Black's queen lands beside the white king, protected by the black king. White has no square and cannot take her.

steps.caption: In a corner the king has only three neighbours, so there is less to count.

line.say: The queen takes the middle neighbour, protected by the king on b3. The king on a1 has nowhere to go.

steps.caption: White to move: mate in two. The queen cuts the king off, then the white king protects the final check.

line.say: The queen covers the whole seventh rank. The black king has one square left.
Black's only legal move is the king to g8.
Check. The white king on f6 protects the queen, so the king cannot take her. Checkmate.

steps.caption: The queen sits on the seventh rank, but her own king stands in the way. One king move can fix two things at once.

line.say: The king steps off the rank. That opens the queen's line to h7, and the king now covers g7.
The queen goes beside the king on a square the white king protects. Checkmate.

steps.caption: Black's king is boxed in the corner. White's king is two steps away, and the queen is already far off.

line.say: The king steps up to the second rank, where it covers b1, b2 and b3.
The black king goes to a2, its only free square.
The queen checks along the a-file from far away. The king on c2 covers the squares beside the black king. Checkmate.
